summary: Built M2-S03 (access, design-only, owner metadata-builder) into five files: three minimal base Profile files, a single-type package.xml at API 62.0 with bare Profile members, and deploy-order.md. Each profile carries only the residue Q7 names - applicationVisibilities/standard__Service with default=true, two recordTypeVisibilities entries (one default=true), and three layoutAssignments (the fall-through assignment plus one per Case record type) - and no objectPermissions, fieldPermissions, userPermissions, tabVisibilities, loginHours or loginIpRanges. This closes M1 finding F-01: until this step no layoutAssignments element existed anywhere under artefacts/, so check_record_type_layouts.py --manifest-dir artefacts had nothing to cross-check. It now resolves 9 layout-assignment and 12 record-type references and exits 0 on 0 findings over 15 files, while a negative fixture exits 1 - the assertion is live rather than vacuous. All three checkers exited 0 on the first pass with zero repair passes; check-outputs is ok on all five declared outputs with no undeclared file.
confidence_rationale: Step 10: HIGH on four of five conditions - every emitted element name and enum value traces to the Step 3 inventory built from the two cited skills' metadata-examples.md files, all three checkers exited 0 on the first pass with no repair pass, check-outputs returned ok, and every declared output was written with nothing undeclared and nothing outside artefacts/M2-S03/. MEDIUM because the fifth is not met: two of the ten deduplicated Questions-to-Ask rows were not answered from the plan (managed-package dependency, and whether Person Accounts are enabled) and took a documented skill default or an omission, and because three of the nine layout assignments written depend on a platform behaviour neither cited skill documents - whether a layoutAssignments entry is accepted for a record type the same profile marks visible=false. That is recorded as ungrounded in deploy-order.md rather than asserted.

dimensions_skipped.reason: Two of the ten deduplicated Questions-to-Ask rows across the two cited skills were not answered from plan.json. 'Does a managed package require this profile to be assigned?' has no answer and no managed package appears in requirement.md or any of the 97 clarifications, so no exception list was written. 'Are Person Accounts enabled on this org?' is unanswered, so personAccountDefault was omitted rather than guessed. Neither is a query failure; both are recorded in deploy-order.md.

Three facts the emitted files depend on are not settled by the cited skills and are recorded as UNGROUNDED in deploy-order.md rather than asserted: (1) whether the Profile deploy enforces element sequence inside the root - the two cited examples order the same elements differently, and alphabetical was chosen because it matches a retrieve; (2) whether a layoutAssignments entry is accepted for a record type the same profile marks visible=false - the guide text the skills quote covers only the inactive-record-type case, and both record types here are active; (3) whether Person Accounts are enabled, which bounds (2) and the omitted personAccountDefault. Every element NAME and enum value written is grounded; these are behaviours, not names.

process_observations.observation: All three checkers exited 0 on the first pass with zero repair passes, and check_access_model.py returns 1 on ANY finding rather than on a severity threshold - so its zero-finding result is a positive statement that no migratable permission was left on these profiles.

The build-scope layout checker now resolves 9 layoutAssignment references and 12 record-type references against M1-S01's record types and M1-S02's layouts; a negative fixture naming Case-Ghost Layout and Case.Nonexistent exits 1 under --strict, so the exit code carries a real cross-reference rather than a silent pass.

Q11's answer ('clone Standard User into custom profiles') is superseded by the cited skill's own gotcha: at API 60.0 and later a profile that does not exist in the target org is seeded from Minimum Access - Salesforce, and Standard User applies only at 59.0 and earlier. This manifest is 62.0, so the answer names a behaviour the platform no longer has - and the behaviour it does have is the better one for a permission-set-led model.

Profile deployment overlays rather than replaces, so if the target org already carries profiles named 'Acme Support Tier 1', 'Acme Support Tier 2' or 'Acme Billing', whatever those profiles grant today survives this deploy silently - these three minimal files create a minimal profile only on a create, never on an overlay.

Whether the Metadata API accepts a layoutAssignments entry for a record type the same profile marks visible=false is not addressed by either cited skill; the guide text they quote covers only the inactive-record-type case, and both record types here are active. Three of the nine layout assignments written depend on the answer.

The record-types skill asks whether Person Accounts are enabled and no clarification in plan.json answers it, so personAccountDefault was omitted rather than written with a guessed value; the element is documented as inert when Person Accounts is off.

Element ordering inside the Profile root is not settled by the cited skills - the record-types example is alphabetical and the permission-sets-vs-profiles example is not - so alphabetical was chosen because it matches what a Metadata API retrieve returns, and no mock deploy in this build has yet exercised a Profile.

A mock deploy over M2 would settle the two ungrounded Profile facts this step recorded (element ordering, and layoutAssignments on a not-visible record type) at the cost of one dry-run rather than one production incident.
